title: Route Selector Forensics Playbook — sampled per-hop frames & interactive replay
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Build a playbook and implementation for 'Route Selector Forensics' — a storage and UX pattern that captures sampled per-hop snapshots (frames) of routing decisions, light-weight contextual artifacts, and an interactive replay UI to reconstruct request routing paths across region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants. The goal is to enable fast root-cause analysis for production incidents and user-impacting regressions without retaining full payloads or incurring large storage costs.

Problem: When a request experiences higher latency or a quality regression we frequently need to know: which region/tier/model variant was chosen, what decision rationale (policy predicates, cost/latency scoring) influenced that choice, and what were the per-hop micro-metrics (queue wait, batch size, variant fallback reason). Existing traces capture some spans but are noisy, lack compact contextual snapshots, and are either too verbose or throw away useful decision artifacts.

Goals: 
- Capture a compact, privacy-safe per-hop snapshot (frame) for routed requests, with sample controls and TTL-based retention.
- Keep CPU and I/O overhead bounded: use adaptive sampling, per-customer rate caps, and size-limited artifacts (<= 8KB compressed/frame target).
- Provide an interactive replay tool in Console to step through frames and visualize decision tree, latencies and fallback triggers.
- Support deterministic replay for debugging (snapshots include normalized hashes and non-sensitive config references rather than full user data).
- Instrument cost and SLO impact per recorded path for triage and RCA.

Scope & Non-goals: 
- Includes: routing metadata capture, per-hop micro-metrics, adaptive sampling controller, frame storage schema, replay API and Console UI surface, access controls.
- Excludes: full request/response payload capture, long-term raw trace archival (we will link to existing traces instead).

Design proposal (high level): 
1) Frame schema (compact): {artifact_id, timestamp, route_key, selected_region, selected_tier, model_variant, decision_score_vector_ref, fallback_reason_code (optional), micro_metrics: {queue_ms, scheduling_ms, kernel_ms, kvcache_hit_rate_pct, batch_size}, feature_flags_snapshot_ref, normalized_prompt_hash (salted), sampling_reason, sampling_seed}. Frames are serialized into a compact binary blob and gzip compressed. We will avoid storing PII by design: only salted hashes and config references.

2) Sampling strategy: 
- Default reservoir sampling: 1 in N requests per tenant, with a hard per-tenant/day cap. 
- Adaptive upsampling: if a request triggers an SLO breach (latency>p95 threshold) or a model fallback, it is guaranteed to be captured (subject to cap).
- Manual capture: Console/SDK can request a one-off capture for a specific request id (needs elevated ACL).

3) Storage & retention: 
- Short-lived object store (S3) with lifecycle rule: 30 days hot -> 90 days warm (index only) -> delete.
- Postgres index table stores artifact_id, tenant_id, route_key, timestamp, sampling_reason, and small JSON metadata for fast queries. Actual frames in object store.
- Encryption-at-rest using KMS keys (customer-managed for Private deployments).

4) Access controls & privacy: 
- Role-based access via Console; only users with "routing_forensics" privilege can view full frames. 
- Audit log events for frame reads.
- For Private deployments, frames inherit tenant KMS policy and cannot be exported externally by default.

5) Replay UX & APIs: 
- Backend replay API rehydrates frames and fetches linked config references (policy definitions, model manifest) to reconstruct the decision path. 
- Console UI shows timeline with per-hop micro-metrics, a compact textual rationale (policy predicates evaluated true/false), and a diff view between attempted variant and selected variant for fallback cases. 
- Support export of a sanitized 'incident bundle' (redacted frames + links) for handoffs.

6) Instrumentation & metrics: 
- New SLI/SLO: fraction of customer-impacting routing incidents with at least one captured frame within 5m of incident start. Target: 95%.
- Metrics emitted: frames_captured_total{reason}, frame_capture_size_bytes_summary, frames_replayed_total, replay_latency_ms_p90.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Storing full traces vs compact frames: frames limit storage and privacy but may omit low-level kernel traces; we will link to full traces when available for deep dives.
- Sampling caps vs guaranteed capture: ensure we still can capture critical incidents via adaptive upsampling, accepting some cost variance.
- Index in Postgres vs ElasticSearch: Postgres preferred for simpler transactional guarantees and existing infra familiarity; we will add an async indexer for full-text needs if queries show it necessary.

Implementation plan (milestones): 
A. Schema & ingestion hooks (2 sprints): introduce Frame protobuf, RPC hook points in routing decision service, basic compressor.
B. Sampling controller & tenant quotas (1 sprint): implement reservoir + adaptive rules and admin controls into Console.
C. Storage & indexer (1 sprint): S3 writer + Postgres index table + lifecycle policy.
D. Replay API & basic Console feature (2 sprints): backend rehydration + timeline UI with per-hop metrics.
E. Security review, load testing, canary rollout (1 sprint).

Backward compatibility & rollout: Start with a low global sample rate for hosted API (0.01%) and opt-in per-tenant higher sampling. Gate by runtime flag and feature rollout per region. Canary in us-west first.

Monitoring & validation: Synthetic jobs to exercise routing variants and generate frames; validate size, correctness, and that adaptive upsamples are captured. Run load tests to validate <5% added p99 latency to routing decision path.

Open questions / TODOs: 
- Decide final compression format (snappy vs gzip) following perf tests.
- Confirm TTL policy for self-hosted customers per contract.
- UX mockups: attach design spec link.

- Confluence PRD: https://rwd.atl/confluence/display/INF/Route+Selector+Forensics+PRD (draft)
- Design mocks: https://drive.google.com/designs/route-forensics-mockup
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-service/pull/12345
acceptance_criteria: Frames can be produced by the routing service with size <= 8KB compressed for 95% of captured frames
Adaptive upsampling captures 100% of requests that trigger a model fallback or exceed latency SLO during the test window
Console displays replay timeline and per-hop micro-metrics for a sample incident within 2s of request for warm cache
Access controls prevent users without 'routing_forensics' role from viewing raw frames; audit events are emitted for reads
End-to-end load test shows <5% increase in routing decision p99 latency at target sample rates
